overview: The Vijayanagara Empire was a major Hindu state that resisted Islamic expansion and fostered Dravidian culture for over three centuries. Its capital at Hampi became one of the world's largest and most prosperous cities before its catastrophic destruction.

items.text: Dravidian temple architecture reaches its zenith with elaborate gopurams and pillared halls.
The Virupaksha and Vittala temples at Hampi exemplify the Vijayanagara style.
Literature in Telugu, Kannada, Tamil and Sanskrit flourished under royal patronage.
International trade in spices, textiles, gems and horses with Portuguese, Arab and Chinese merchants.
Foreign travelers described the capital's bazaars as among the world's most magnificent.
The city's population estimated at 500,000, making it one of the largest cities in the world.
Sophisticated irrigation systems supported intensive agriculture in the Tungabhadra valley.
Hampi ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage site with over 1,600 surviving monuments.
Hindu temple building traditions continued in southern India after the empire's fall.

fall.text: After the catastrophic Battle of Talikota in 1565, the empire gradually fragmented and disappeared by 1646.
